scope: 87 behavior cases, 12 named scenarios, 31 browser-equivalent journeys. Documentation-only audit of existing evidence at a frozen native checkpoint.

definitions.mapped-existing-evidence: The listed assertions have cited historical native evidence. This is a mapping, not a fresh candidate pass or a blanket acceptance of every sentence in the original case.
definitions.partial: An explicit assertion remains without matching native evidence in the inspected receipts. A gap is not automatically an implementation defect.
definitions.composed-partial: Related assertions are covered across receipts, but the named scenario/profile has no complete native execution certificate.

boundaries: No new tests, provider calls, process launches, active-data changes or release acceptance performed during this audit.
Scripted providers exercise real native control flow, Git, Docker, OMP and Mail only where each receipt says so. No live-provider/model-quality claim.
Five positive GPUI journeys at the frozen checkpoint use explicitly stopped attempt records and real service/Git/loopback providers; not live model execution.
Historical source manifests remain authoritative for each execution. A newer aggregate Rust test count does not rerun old expensive fixtures. Final combined release revalidation is separate.
Retained browser/domain evidence is not native UI proof; documented failures and focused retries remain as recorded.
New main-branch work after the frozen checkpoint is intentionally excluded; root owns UI closure, terminal focus/accessibility integration and cutover.

cases.title: Site-aware upsert
cases.expected: Two tasks remain distinct; only that site's imported fields change; local notes, criteria and history survive.
assertionsCovered: Site and issue IDs remain distinct
imported fields update independently of local refinements and history.

cases.title: Board and queue order
cases.expected: Board follows imported rank; execution order follows local priority.
assertionsCovered: Saved-filter order is retained
local queue order has separate transactional control
Jira outage preserves last complete snapshot.

cases.title: Optional Explore and Grill
cases.expected: Direct Run is allowed; Explore/Grill persist notes without launching coding work.
assertionsCovered: Direct coding admission is supported
Explore and Grill run a coordinator and save proposals without coding work
native accept/discard controls persist decisions.

cases.title: Accepted brief versions
cases.expected: Queued and active snapshots retain their versions; changed scope requires an explicit decision before affected work continues.
assertionsCovered: Captured brief versions survive changes
active adoption requires a reason

obsolete insertion is rejected.

cases.title: Conflicting Jira refresh
cases.expected: Affected work pauses for a decision; neither side silently overwrites the other.
assertionsCovered: Conflicting source requirements preserve accepted local scope and hold active work
repeated conflict observation does not repeatedly clean up or repair.

cases.title: Explicit repository scope
cases.expected: One target is required per coding ticket; mappings never change silently; no cross-repository dispatch.
assertionsCovered: One captured target governs admission and worktree preparation
retired target prevents queueing until explicit active replacement.

cases.title: Research-only outcome
cases.expected: Produce the requested artifact and limitations; no fabricated commit, coding check or PR is required.
assertionsCovered: Pinned research checks real citations and artifacts
verified/rejected/superseded history survives reopen
completion requires stopped ownership and no coding records.

cases.title: No automatic backlog execution
cases.expected: Only the selected item starts; duplicate requests do not create duplicate active runs.
assertionsCovered: Durable queue admission is idempotent
only selected plans are queued
no agents appear when runner capability is unavailable.

cases.title: Minimal versus complex team
cases.expected: Small work uses a small team; complex work admits justified specialists within scheduler limits; neither launches the whole catalog.
assertionsCovered: Selected teams require validated proposals and respect three-specialist ceiling
disabled or unjustified selections fail before admission.

cases.title: Custom role lifecycle
cases.expected: Validation is enforced; a valid inserted role gets a real assignment at a safe point; disabled roles cannot receive new work.
assertionsCovered: Role creation/edit/disable uses revisions
native edits and conflicts preserve drafts
insertion waits for a safe point and creates explicit replacement identities.

cases.title: Immutable definition snapshot
cases.expected: Existing assignment keeps its definition/model revision; only a new explicit assignment uses the update.
assertionsCovered: Role/model definitions are copied into immutable assignment snapshots
later role versions affect only explicitly new assignments.

cases.title: Project constraints
cases.expected: Each assignment includes its own project constraints; reusable defaults remain unchanged.
assertionsCovered: Each host profile receives captured project instructions and role constraints
project guidance approval does not rewrite reusable role defaults.

cases.title: Reviewer independence
cases.expected: Self-review cannot satisfy the gate; a separate non-implementer assignment can, even with the same model.
assertionsCovered: Reviewer assignment/session must be independent of every implementing author
readiness requires current independent review.

cases.title: Reporter versus writer
cases.expected: Reporter uses bounded Jira permissions; writer edits only its authorized repository scope and respects the single-writer lease.
assertionsCovered: Reporter authority gates controller-derived Jira writes
repository mutation needs an owned scope and single-writer lease.

cases.title: Invalid selection proposal

assertionsCovered: Unknown/disabled/duplicate/infrastructure selections and unavailable roles are refused before privileged launch

cases.title: Missing, stale and ambiguous selectors

cases.title: Default model resolution

cases.title: Capabilities and context limits

cases.title: Runtime identity mismatch

cases.title: Explicit fallback

cases.title: Advisory router boundaries

cases.title: Secondary OMP model paths

cases.title: Provider error taxonomy

assertionsCovered: 401/403/429, timeouts, disconnects and malformed/empty responses are classified

cases.title: Four-hop external round trip

assertionsCovered: Durable addressed records and one actual OMP/Rust Mail peer handoff are proved

cases.title: Passive observer

cases.title: Duplicate delivery

cases.title: Reordering and causality

cases.title: Lost send acknowledgement

cases.title: Receive crash windows
cases.expected: Durable inbox/application records support recovery; no loss or repeated side effect at any window.
assertionsCovered: Five actual Mail receive interruption windows cover durable inbox, application and acknowledgement recovery without duplicate domain effects.

cases.title: Mailbox restart and expiration
cases.expected: Reconnect with bounded backoff; retention/idempotency limits are visible; expiry does not mean delivered or task complete.
assertionsCovered: Unavailable/restarted Mail holds admission, reconnects with bounds and retains pending work

cases.title: Routing and isolation
cases.expected: Reject or quarantine unauthorized routing; never wake the wrong assignment.
assertionsCovered: Current immutable host authority and sender/run/attempt routing reject forged or cross-run actions before effects.

cases.title: Polling and payload boundaries
cases.expected: Respect bounded poll/backoff policy; preserve pending messages; reject invalid payloads; no busy loop.
assertionsCovered: Singleflight polling, round-robin bounds, 429/backoff and payload validation retain pending work without unbounded polls.

cases.title: Process independence
cases.expected: Distinct OS processes and sessions remain observable; surviving agents continue or wait according to dependency state.
assertionsCovered: Independent host/runner OS identities remain observable

cases.title: Specialist replacement
cases.expected: Resume a usable session or create a new attempt with saved handoff; preserve work; reject stale prior ownership/results.
assertionsCovered: Actual OMP usable-session restoration and wrong/empty session fallback are tested

cases.title: Coordinator restart

assertionsCovered: Durable message dispatch receipts and current host identities reconcile after controller death before a repeated effect.

cases.title: Workbench restart

cases.title: Resume and cancellation

cases.title: PID reuse and competing owners

cases.title: Recovery bounds

cases.title: Partial and corrupt state

cases.title: Single writer lease
